script: "New kid's uncle stole our games… and the next day he sent us a fake letter that left us all stunned.". I was a teenager in the 90s, and PC gaming was basically a scavenger hunt. We'd buy copies from abroad through airmail—expensive, but better than nothing—then trade and rip off the copy protection so we could play more for less. A new kid rolled into our class, and his uncle had a library of games we didn't even know existed. We swapped our originals for his, thinking it'd be fair. Instead, we got corrupted floppies, missing copy protection, and after months of trade, we had zero working titles while he kept all our Settlers, Doom II, Monkey Island, etc. He even returned some in worse shape. We were done. Fast forward to the AIDS awareness event the school hosted. The foundation handed out flyers and condoms with their logo. We snagged a bunch because we knew where the trouble was headed. We had a computer and an inkjet at home, so we cooked up a fake letter to the new kid, mimicking the foundation's font and logo. It read something like: "Dear FIRST NAME, Thank you for your letter. We understand it's difficult being open about being homosexual, and you have many questions after the event you attended with your class. Please find enclosed a flyer that should answer many of your questions, as well as some condoms. Please practice safe sex at all times." We mailed it to "Mr. LASTNAME" so his dad would open it first. The fallout was insane. His mother cried, his dad was fuming, and the kid was grounded for weeks, convinced he was gay. He figured we were behind it because we'd been watching his reactions. When we finally confessed, we had to explain our prank to the principal with his parents in the room. It was the best revenge I ever pulled, even though it was 30 years ago.
